objective: Improve geometric-mean mimalloc operations per second on four frozen deterministic single-thread, four-thread, small-object, and fragmentation workloads. The pinned upstream api/api-fill/stress suite, deterministic checksums, a four-thread maximum, peak allocator page-committed bytes, and live-page fragmentation at or below the split baseline plus 1% are hard gates. Only allocator implementation files under src and internal headers under include/mimalloc are mutable; trusted statistics and all build, test, evaluator, and workload code are protected.

meta.provenance: microsoft/mimalloc at exact revision 76d3f8a934f9761e4ee75fa8b071e58d482f2758; four independently authored protected C workload drivers use sealed deterministic xorshift64-v1 seeds; terminal holdout received no optimizer, mutation, or headroom pilot; token-locked interleaved fresh-process A-A samples [77346185.25585209,76981204.4984155,76780373.53483647] give qBase=77035921.09636801 and sample sigma=286846.91993864416; qReference=77035921.09636801+max(5*286846.91993864416,0.05*abs(77035921.09636801-0))=80887717.15118642

mutableEnvelope: src/** except src/stats.c, src/static.c, and src/alloc-override.c

measurement.platform: linux/arm64 Docker Desktop on Apple M3 Max; final recalibration required on frozen GCE Linux host
measurement.q: geometric mean operations per second across single, multithread, small, and fragmentation drivers
measurement.benchmarkSampleSelection: fastest of 5 timed samples per workload (k=1 trimmed selection; host contention can only lengthen a sample, so the minimum elapsed time rejects scheduler-noise outliers without candidate-controlled influence)
measurement.peakCommittedGate: for each workload, mi_stats_get page_committed.peak after a fresh mi_stats_reset and fixed one-round memory pass must be <= split baseline * 1.01
measurement.fragmentationGate: at each driver's fixed live allocation checkpoint, max(0,page_committed.current-(malloc_normal.current+malloc_huge.current))/page_committed.current from merged mi_stats must be <= split baseline * 1.01

exploitReview.protectedPathEscape: broker diff-protects build files, public/statistics headers, statistics implementation, evaluator, worker, tests, and four workload drivers; evaluator rejects symlinks and new files outside src or include/mimalloc
exploitReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: distinct sealed train and validation seeds; a trusted first-size fingerprint diagnostic is expected to win train and lose validation
exploitReview.fixtureFingerprinting: both split configurations are holdout-only and mounted under root-owned /capsule; compilation runs as uid 2000 before the protected evaluator invokes drivers
exploitReview.outputFabrication: trusted drivers perform real mi_malloc/mi_zalloc/mi_free calls, touch allocation boundaries, and emit deterministic non-address checksums checked against sealed values; the trusted evaluator additionally audits every linked benchmark binary with nm and rejects candidate-defined timing or output symbols (clock_gettime, printf, write and variants), and runs each workload under a kernel-enforced RLIMIT_NPROC task cap of the sealed thread budget plus the coordinating main thread
exploitReview.buildScriptMutation: CMake files, fixed O2/MI_STAT flags, worker, test sources, and toolchain lock are protected; every evaluation performs a clean source rebuild
exploitReview.timerTampering: protected harness reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW through a non-interposable inline direct-syscall boundary (no linkable timing symbol exists for a candidate translation unit to interpose), runs under uid 2000 with network disabled, and the evaluator's symbol audit rejects any candidate-defined timing or output symbols before a benchmark binary is executed
exploitReview.deadCodeBenchmarkBypass: the benchmark uses public allocation entry points linked to the same static library exercised by upstream api and stress tests
